name: Morgan Advanced Materials plc
executive_summary: Morgan Advanced Materials plc (MGAM.L) is a UK-listed advanced materials group serving industrial, aerospace, semiconductor, energy and healthcare end-markets through three divisions: Performance Carbon, Technical Ceramics and Thermal Products. The quantitative screen rates the name a **buy** (5/22 models; composite 77%), chiefly on **cheapness** and **risk** metrics — notably FCF yield (~7.2%), Acquirer's Multiple, Magic Formula and Earnings Quality — with a 4.8% dividend yield and P/B of 2.2. Filings show a cyclical trough in FY2025 (headline adjusted margin 9.6%; statutory continuing EPS loss of 1.0p) followed by H1 2026 stabilisation (OCC revenue +4.8%; adjusted margin 11.2%), portfolio simplification (MMS disposal; Thermal Products strategic review), and a self-help roadmap targeting 12% margin by 2028. The central debate is whether cash-flow-based cheapness and simplification savings outweigh weak reported earnings, elevated leverage (2.0x net debt/EBITDA at H1 2026), transformation execution risk, and technically extended timing (RSI 82).
investment_thesis:
For a value investor, MGAM offers a cash-generative industrial franchise trading below intrinsic measures implied by the screen, with identifiable self-help levers not fully reflected in trailing statutory earnings.

**Quantitative alignment.** The screen passes five models across cheapness and risk families with high data quality (19/20 metrics). FCF of £50.7m (Yahoo; filing headline FCF £45.4m for FY2025) supports a ~7.2% FCF yield on enterprise value — the primary valuation hook. Dividend yield of 4.8% with dividend maintained at 12.2p (FY2025) and 5.4p interim (H1 2026) adds income support. P/B of 2.2 is reasonable for a materials business with £984.8m total assets and tangible book of £149.7m (Yahoo FY2025).

**Business quality beneath the screen.** Morgan combines material science and application engineering across ~57 sites and ~8,100 employees, with low customer concentration (no customer >5% of revenue, per H1 2026 filing). Aerospace & Defence, Energy and Technical Ceramics showed resilience through the downturn; simplification has delivered £24m cumulative adjusted operating profit benefits vs a 2023 baseline, tracking toward £27m by end-2026. ROIC of 14.1% (FY2025 filing) remains respectable despite margin compression.

**Why buy, not pass.** The screen correctly identifies a business generating solid operating cash (£168.6m FY2025; £43.3m H1 2026) while statutory earnings are depressed by one-offs: £47.6m specific adjusting items in FY2025 (semiconductor impairment £15.6m, ERP £13.3m, restructuring), plus fair-value volatility on MMS disposal consideration shares. Normalised adjusted EPS of 15.9p (FY2025) and 10.7p (H1 2026) better reflect underlying economics. Management's medium-term framework — 12–14% margins, 17–20% ROIC, leverage 1.0–1.5x — offers a credible re-rating path if execution lands.

**Caveat on timing.** The screen flags neutral timing: RSI 82, price 17% above the 200-day MA. Value entry is supported fundamentally; near-term technicals suggest patience on sizing.
financial_review:
*Sources: Full Year Results (3 March 2026), Half-year Financial Report (6 August 2026), AGM Trading Update (7 May 2026). Yahoo (`financials_annual.json`) cited only where noted.*

**FY2025 — annual (Full Year Results, year ended 31 December 2025)**

| Metric | FY2025 | FY2024 | Change |
|--------|--------|--------|--------|
| Headline revenue | £1,030.3m | £1,100.7m | -6.4% (-3.3% OCC) |
| Continuing revenue | £996.6m | £1,060.1m | -6.0% |
| Headline adjusted operating profit | £99.1m | £128.4m | -22.8% |
| Headline adjusted margin | 9.6% | 11.7% | -210 bps |
| Statutory operating profit (continuing) | £45.2m | £99.2m | -54.4% |
| Adjusted EPS | 15.9p | 24.2p | -34.3% |
| Basic EPS (continuing) | (1.0)p | 16.5p | n/m |
| Cash from operations | £168.6m | £163.0m | +3.4% |
| Headline free cash flow | £45.4m | £15.1m | +200.7% |
| Net debt | £232.2m | £226.2m | +2.7% |
| Net debt/EBITDA (ex. IFRS 16) | 1.8x headline / 1.9x continuing | 1.4x / 1.5x | elevated |
| ROIC | 14.1% | 17.7% | -360 bps |
| Dividend per share | 12.2p | 12.2p | flat (cover 1.3x adj. EPS) |

Revenue weakness reflected semiconductor (-8.9% OCC in Performance Carbon), European industrial softness and healthcare inventory destocking, partly offset by aerospace strength. Margin fell 210 bps headline, with volume/mix (-440 bps) partly offset by pricing/efficiency (+170 bps) and simplification (+160 bps). Statutory profit was further hit by £47.6m specific adjusting items, including a £15.6m semiconductor asset impairment and ongoing ERP spend.

**Discontinued operations:** MMS disposal completed 12 November 2025 for total consideration £76.2m (cash £20.5m plus ~£55.7m FIL shares); gain on disposal £28.5m. FY2025 profit from discontinued operations £23.7m.

**Balance sheet (31 December 2025, filing):** Total assets £984.8m; equity £348.9m; net debt £232.2m; cash £79.3m; undrawn RCF headroom £295.3m; total liquidity headroom £369.5m. Scheduled maturities October 2026: $97m and €25m, expected to be refinanced from existing facilities.

**H1 2026 — interim (Half-year Report, six months ended 30 June 2026)**

| Metric | H1 2026 | H1 2025 (restated) | Change |
|--------|---------|---------------------|--------|
| Revenue | £518.1m | £502.5m | +3.1% (+4.8% OCC) |
| Adjusted operating profit | £57.8m | £54.8m | +5.5% (+7.2% OCC) |
| Adjusted margin | 11.2% | 10.9% | +30 bps |
| Adjusted EPS | 10.7p | 9.9p | +8.1% |
| Statutory operating profit | £39.1m | £41.6m | -6.0% |
| Cash from continuing operations | £43.3m | £70.3m | -38.4% |
| Free cash flow | £3.5m | £4.6m | -23.9% |
| Net debt | £253.1m | £249.1m | +1.6% |
| Net debt/EBITDA | 2.0x | 1.8x | elevated |
| Interim dividend | 5.4p | 5.4p | maintained |

H1 showed broad revenue recovery: Technical Ceramics +7.8% OCC (aerospace/engine components), Performance Carbon +4.0% OCC, Thermal Products +2.5% OCC. Margin included a non-recurring £8.9m semiconductor take-or-pay phasing benefit (~160 bps); excluding this, OCC revenue growth was ~3.0%. Thermal Products margin fell to 6.4% on US operational issues; a site turnaround is underway.

**Trading update (7 May 2026):** Q1 2026 OCC revenue +6.2% vs weak prior-year comparator; full-year 2026 guidance maintained (OCC revenue growth ~2%; H2 margin broadly in line with H1 ex phasing).

**Trend assessment.** Revenue and margins troughed in FY2025 and are recovering sequentially, but reported earnings remain noisy and H1 FCF was weak (£3.5m) on working-capital phasing. Leverage rose to 2.0x at H1 2026 (above management's 1.0–1.5x target range), with management guiding reduction toward ~1.7x in H2 as FCF normalises and MMS proceeds are realised (FIL shares valued £48.8m at 30 June 2026).

**Gaps.** Four of seven annual filings in the index lack downloadable body text (Companies House accounts 2022–2024). The 26 March 2026 Annual Financial Report RNS is a publication notice only — no additional financial detail beyond the 3 March Full Year Results. No separate prior-year interim filing body is indexed beyond H1 2026.

**Yahoo fallback (FY2025 only, where filing-aligned):** Yahoo revenue £996.6m, FCF £50.7m, net debt £231.8m, operating cash flow £117.8m — broadly consistent with filing figures; Yahoo statutory net income £21.1m includes discontinued operations.
risks_and_flags:
**Cyclical and end-market exposure.** Semiconductor, European industrial and automotive markets drove FY2025 weakness; supply-chain shift toward China prompted a £15.6m UK asset impairment. End-markets have stabilised but remain sensitive to capex cycles and geopolitics (management flagged emerging Middle East risk in FY2025 results, though Q1 2026 trading update reported no material impact).

**Margin and transformation execution.** Adjusted margin fell from 11.7% to 9.6% in FY2025; recovery to 12% by 2028 requires ERP rollout (£22–24m expected in 2026 alone), site turnarounds, and Group-led procurement — all while Thermal Products (6.4% H1 margin) undergoes strategic review. Failure to deliver would leave the stock cheap for a reason.

**Leverage and liquidity.** Net debt/EBITDA at 2.0x (H1 2026) exceeds the stated 1.0–1.5x framework. Covenants permit up to 3.0x net debt/EBITDA and minimum 4.0x interest cover (filings confirm compliance and going concern for 18 months). October 2026 bond maturities ($97m, €25m) require refinancing — manageable given £347.7m undrawn facility headroom at H1, but not immaterial.

**Portfolio and accounting complexity.** MMS disposal consideration held as FVTPL equity (£48.8m at 30 June 2026) creates ongoing fair-value volatility in specific adjusting items. Dividend cover at 1.3x adjusted EPS (FY2025) is below the 2.5x target — dividend maintained but not obviously secure on a normalised basis without recovery.

**Governance and key person.** CEO Damien Caby appointed July 2025; CFO Richard Armitage announced intention to retire (7 May 2026 RNS, body not downloaded). Buyback paused after £20m of £40m programme to preserve balance sheet resilience.

**Pension.** Defined benefit obligations on balance sheet (£12.4m asset / £34.4m liability non-current at FY2025); net IAS 19 interest £0.4m FY2025. Actuarial sensitivity noted in filings — not a dominant risk but present.

**Safety.** Lost-time accident rate rose to 0.18 from 0.13 (FY2025), flagged as a Board priority.

**Going concern (filing language):** Directors confirm reasonable expectation of adequate resources for at least 18 months; reverse stress test suggests EBITDA would need to fall ~30% combined with 30% net debt increase before covenant breach — deemed implausible given end-market diversity.

RiskTags: cyclical, leverage, competitive, governance, pension, accounting, other
news_highlights:
News coverage over the past year is moderate — dominated by results, strategy updates and syndicated market commentary rather than deep investigative coverage.

**Results and guidance**
- *Morgan Advanced Materials shares drop as weaker end markets drag on earnings* (Yahoo Finance UK, 3 March 2026) — market reaction to FY2025 margin compression.
- *Morgan Advanced Materials H1 Earnings Call Highlights* (Yahoo Finance, 6 August 2026) — H1 revenue +4.8% OCC, margin 11.2%, full-year outlook maintained; CEO Damien Caby cited in-line performance amid softer European industrial conditions.
- *MGAM: Revenue up 4.8% year-over-year, margin at 11.2%* (TradingView, 6 August 2026) — syndicated H1 summary.

**Strategy and portfolio**
- FY2025 results (3 March 2026) and H1 2026 (6 August 2026): strategic review of Thermal Products division underway, options include potential disposal; MMS sale completed November 2025; December 2025 strategy update targeting 12% margin by 2028.
- *AGM Trading Update* (7 May 2026): Q1 OCC revenue +6.2%; full-year 2026 guidance maintained; strategic review progressing.

**Management**
- CFO Richard Armitage intention to retire (RNS headline, 7 May 2026 — body not in corpus).
- Damien Caby became CEO July 2025 (referenced in FY2025 results).

**Corporate actions**
- Share buyback: £20m completed of £40m programme; paused December 2025 for balance sheet resilience.
- Dividend maintained; simplywall.st cautioned against ex-dividend chasing (4 April 2026).

**Thin areas:** Limited sell-side or investigative coverage in the manifest; several Kalkine Media pieces are generic FTSE context. No material M&A beyond MMS disposal or regulatory enforcement actions captured.
research_rationale: Deep research confirms the screen's FCF-based cheapness and simplification optionality, but partially weakens the buy case on depressed statutory earnings, elevated leverage, transformation execution risk, and overbought technical timing.
